title: Runtime Visualization Substrate
context: UI performance bottlenecks were identified as DOM lifecycle churn (teardown/rebuild) rather than SVG throughput. Exploratory sprint UI-R1 proved that a retained patching model eliminates this churn while preserving semantic identity.
decisions: Transition from imperative redraw to retained render graph.
Introduce SceneGraphManager for retention and garbage collection.
Preserve SVG as the primary substrate for accessibility and style integrity.
Bind visual element identity to authoritative Projection IDs.

positive: Significant reduction in DOM mutation and layout thrashing.
Persistence of visual state (selection, animation) across updates.
Stable accessibility tree for screen readers.
Clear architectural seam for future non-DOM renderers (Canvas/WebGPU).
negative: Increased logic complexity for state diffing and patching.
Risk of visual/DOM state desync if patch logic is incomplete.
